Reproducible figures: embedded data and logging

Source: vignettes/reproducibility.Rmd
reproducibility.Rmd

Figure files tend to outlive the scripts that made them. ggsaveR offers two ways to keep track of where a figure came from: embedding information in the PNG file itself, and keeping a log of every file saved.

library(ggplot2)
library(ggsaveR)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'ggsaveR'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:ggplot2':
#> 
#>     ggsave

Embedding data in PNG files

With embed_data = TRUE, every PNG file carries the expression passed as plot, the data behind the plot, the printed sessionInfo() and the plot object. The information is stored in the file’s text chunks, so the image looks the same and opens in any viewer.

old <- ggsaveR_options(embed_data = TRUE)

ggsave(
  "versicolor-virginica.png",
  iris |>
    subset(Species != "setosa") |>
    ggplot(aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, colour = Species)) +
    geom_point(),
  width = 6, height = 4
)
#> Embedded reproducibility data into versicolor-virginica.png (140.9 Kb)
options(old)

read_ggsaveR_data() reads the information back:

info <- read_ggsaveR_data("versicolor-virginica.png")
#> 'versicolor-virginica.png' also holds the plot object. Use `trusted = TRUE` to restore it, but only if you trust the file.
cat(info$plot_call)
#> ggplot(subset(iris, Species != "setosa"), aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, 
#>     colour = Species)) + geom_point()
head(info$plot_data)
#>   Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width    Species
#> 1          7.0         3.2          4.7         1.4 versicolor
#> 2          6.4         3.2          4.5         1.5 versicolor
#> 3          6.9         3.1          4.9         1.5 versicolor
#> 4          5.5         2.3          4.0         1.3 versicolor
#> 5          6.5         2.8          4.6         1.5 versicolor
#> 6          5.7         2.8          4.5         1.3 versicolor

When the plot is stored in a variable, as in ggsave("plot.png", p), the recorded expression is just p. The data and plot object are embedded either way.

The plot object

The plot object is stored as a serialized R object. Restoring a serialized object can run arbitrary code, in the same way as readRDS() or load(), so read_ggsaveR_data() only restores it when you confirm that you trust the file:

restored <- read_ggsaveR_data("versicolor-virginica.png", trusted = TRUE)$plot_object
restored + theme_minimal()

The call, session information and data are stored as plain text and CSV, and are always safe to read. Data read from the CSV copy have the column types that read.csv() infers; restored$data has the exact original.

Reading the information outside R

The call and session information are in the text chunks ggsaveR_call and ggsaveR_session, which tools such as exiftool show directly. The data are in ggsaveR_data_csv as a UTF-8 CSV file, compressed with zlib and base64 encoded. In Python:

import base64, io, zlib
import pandas as pd
from PIL import Image

text = Image.open("versicolor-virginica.png").text["ggsaveR_data_csv"]
data = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(text))))

Choosing what to embed

embed_metadata selects the parts: any of "plot", "data", "session_info" and "call". To record only how a figure was made, without its data:

ggsaveR_options(embed_data = TRUE, embed_metadata = c("call", "session_info"))

The plot object and data are left out, with a warning, if together they would add more than embed_max_size bytes (5 MB by default).

Privacy

A PNG with embedded data contains every column of the plot’s data frame, including those not shown. For plots built inside a function, the plot object also carries the objects in that function’s environment. Do not share such files if the data are sensitive. To save one figure without embedding, use guard = TRUE.

Author metadata

The creator option stores a name as the Author field of PNG files, which file managers and image viewers can display:

old <- ggsaveR_options(creator = "Jane Doe, University of Somewhere")
ggsave("signed.png", restored, width = 6, height = 4)
options(old)

A log of saved figures

The log option appends a row to a CSV file for every file saved, including variants. The MD5 checksum shows whether a figure in a manuscript still matches the one the script produced.

old <- ggsaveR_options(log = "figures-log.csv", formats = c("png", "pdf"))

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point()
ggsave("weight.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5)
ggsave("weight-smooth.png", p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x),
       width = 5, height = 3.5)
options(old)

read.csv("figures-log.csv")[, c("file", "device", "width", "height", "dpi", "plot")]
#>                file device width height dpi
#> 1        weight.png    png     5    3.5 300
#> 2        weight.pdf    pdf     5    3.5  NA
#> 3 weight-smooth.png    png     5    3.5 300
#> 4 weight-smooth.pdf    pdf     5    3.5  NA
#>                                              plot
#> 1                                               p
#> 2                                               p
#> 3 p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
#> 4 p + geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
